KL Divergence
A measure of how one probability distribution is different from a second, reference probability distribution.<SEP>A measure of the difference between two probability distributions.<SEP>A measure used to quantify the difference between two probability distributions, incorporated as a regularization term in the methods.<SEP>A measure of how one probability distribution diverges from a second, reference probability distribution.

Maximum Entropy Principle
A principle used to find the distribution with the largest entropy subject to constraints.<SEP>A principle that favors uniform distributions when no other information is available.

GE-FL
A machine learning method that learns from labeled features using generalized expectation criteria.<SEP>A baseline method based on generalization expectation criteria.<SEP>A method that involves labeled features and potentially regularization terms, serving as a baseline for comparison.<SEP>A Generalized Expectation (GE) method that leverages labeled features as prior knowledge.<SEP>Generalized Expectation-Feature Learning.

Information Gain
A method used to calculate the mutual information of features according to document labels to select labeled features.<SEP>A method used to obtain labeled features by calculating the gain of information.

LDA
Latent Dirichlet Allocation, a method used to select features.<SEP>Linear Discriminant Analysis, a method used to select labeled features.<SEP>Latent Dirichlet Allocation.

Movie Dataset
A dataset used for sentiment classification of movie reviews, which can be balanced or unbalanced.<SEP>A dataset used for experiments, described as balanced (1:1 positive:negative) or unbalanced (e.g., 1:4 positive:negative).

Sentiment
A domain or category for text classification.

Web-page
A domain or category for text classification.

Science
A domain or category for text classification.

Medical and Healthcare
A domain or category for text classification.

Bag-of-words
A feature representation method used in text classification.

Stopwords
Common words in a language that are often removed during text preprocessing.

Neutral features
The most frequent words after removing stop words, whose reference distributions are uniformly distributed.<SEP>Common features used as a simple way of regularization without modification of GE-FL.

Cross-validation
A technique for evaluating machine learning models on a limited data sample.

Objective Function
A function to be optimized in a machine learning model.<SEP>The function that a learning algorithm aims to minimize or maximize.

KL Divergence Term
A regularization term added to the objective function based on KL divergence.

Reference Class Distribution
A distribution used as a reference for class distributions in regularization.

Text Classification
A natural language processing task that involves categorizing text into predefined classes.<SEP>A task in natural language processing that assigns categories to text documents.

Labeled Features
A set of features that have associated labels.<SEP>Features that are associated with instance labels, used in various machine learning methods.<SEP>Features that are strong indicators of a specific class and are manually provided to a classifier.<SEP>Features for which the corresponding class labels are known.

Unbalanced Labeled Features
A scenario where the number of labeled features differs across classes.

Unbalanced Datasets
A scenario where the number of documents differs across classes.

Feature Pool
A collection of selected features from which labeled features are drawn.

Topics
In LDA, latent thematic structures discovered in a collection of documents.

Positive Class
A class within a dataset, often referred to in terms of its distribution and feature selection.<SEP>A specific category within a classification task, often representing a positive sentiment.

Negative Class
A class within a dataset, often referred to in terms of its distribution and feature selection.<SEP>A specific category within a classification task, often representing a negative sentiment.

Maximum Entropy
A method or approach that tends to approach a uniform distribution, often used in contrast to methods incorporating true class distribution knowledge.<SEP>A principle that favors uniform distributions when no other information is available.

Accuracy
A metric used to evaluate the performance of a classification model.

Class Distribution
The ratio of different classes within a dataset, which can be balanced or unbalanced.<SEP>The distribution of instances across different classes.<SEP>Information about the proportion of each class in a dataset.<SEP>The proportion of instances belonging to each class in a dataset.

Generalization Expectation Criteria
A criterion used in machine learning, specifically related to the baseline method GE-FL.

Labeled Features for each class
A specific number of labeled features allocated to each distinct class.

Labeled Features of the documents
Labels associated with features derived from document labels.

Generalized Expectation Criteria
A set of criteria used in machine learning for learning from labeled features.<SEP>A framework that formalizes prior knowledge as constraint terms in the objective function.<SEP>A framework used to constrain model expectations in a preferred direction, often used in parameter estimation objectives.

Reference Distribution
The distribution over classes of labeled features.<SEP>A distribution over classes associated with labeled features, denoted by $\hat{p}(y| x_k)$.

Model Predicted Distribution
The distribution over classes predicted by a model.

Model Parameter
Parameters within a model that indicate the importance of a feature to a class.

Softmax
A function that converts a vector of numbers into a probability distribution.

L-BFGS
An optimization algorithm used for parameter estimation.

Constraint Function
A function used in optimization to define constraints.

Indicator Vector
A vector with a 1 at a specific index corresponding to a label and 0 elsewhere.

Instance Annotation
The process of labeling individual instances.<SEP>The process of assigning labels to individual data instances.

Prior Knowledge
Information provided to a model before training.<SEP>Information external to the data that can be incorporated into learning models.<SEP>Knowledge that has been shown to be useful for natural language processing tasks.

Baseball-Hockey Classification Task
A specific classification task involving baseball and hockey.

Neutral Features
Features that are not informative indicators of any class.<SEP>Features that do not provide additional knowledge to the model, potentially leading to bias.

Uniform Distribution
A probability distribution where all outcomes have equal probability.<SEP>A distribution where all outcomes have an equal probability.

Predicted Class Distribution
The distribution of predicted classes for unlabeled data.

Empirical Distribution
The distribution derived from observed data.<SEP>The distribution of input samples in a dataset, denoted by $\tilde{p}({\rm x})$.

Corpus
A collection of text or data.

Preference Class Distribution
A distribution representing a desired class distribution.

Equation 6
The objective function formula: $\mathcal {O} = \sum _{k \in K} KL(\hat{p}(y|x_k) || p_\theta (y | x_k)) + \sum _{y,i} \frac{\theta _{yi}^2}{2 \sigma ^2}$

Equation 9
The objective function formula including neutral features: $\mathcal {O}_{NE} = \mathcal {O} + \sum _{k \in K^{^{\prime }}} KL(\hat{p}_u(y|x_k) || p_\theta (y | x_k))$

Equation 11
The objective function formula including maximum entropy term: $\mathcal {O}_{ME} = \mathcal {O} + \lambda \sum _{y} p(y) \log p(y)$

Class
A category or group to which instances or features can belong.

Word
A fundamental unit of language, often used as a feature in classification tasks.

Instance
A single data point or example.

Distribution
A function that describes the likelihood of different outcomes.

Optimization Problem
A problem that seeks to find the best solution from a set of feasible solutions.

Feature
An individual measurable property or characteristic of a phenomenon being observed.

Natural Language Processing
A field of computer science and artificial intelligence concerned with the interactions between computers and human language.<SEP>A field of computer science and artificial intelligence concerned with the interaction between computers and human language.

Regularization Terms
Additional terms added to the objective function to influence model behavior, such as KL divergence.<SEP>Techniques applied on top of generalized expectation criteria to improve model robustness.

Sports Category
A classification used in text categorization, indicated by words like NBA, player, and basketball.

Sentiment Classification
A text classification task that determines the polarity of text, where words like terrible, boring indicate negative polarity and perfect, exciting suggest positive polarity.

Bayesian Approaches
A class of methods that encode prior knowledge with a prior on parameters.

Latent Output Variables
Variables used to formalize prior knowledge, which can make outputs interpretable.

Neutral Words
Words that are not strong indicators of any specific class and can be used to improve model robustness.

Druck et al.
An entity that explored constraints of labeled features within the GE framework.<SEP>Proposed GE-FL to learn from labeled features using generalized expectation criteria.<SEP>Explored constraints of labeled features in the framework of GE by forcing the model's predicted feature distribution to approach the reference distribution. Proposed an active learning method which solicits labels on features rather than on instances and then used GE-FL to train the model.

Input Samples
Data points used in a model's empirical distribution.

Constraint Functions
Functions used in Generalized Expectation criteria to express preferences on model expectations.

Conditional Model Distribution
The probability distribution of output variables given an input, denoted by $p_\theta (y|\rm x)$.

Score Function
A function used in Generalized Expectation criteria, denoted by $S$.

Parameter Estimation Objective Function
An objective function used in statistical modeling to estimate model parameters.

Input
The data or features fed into a model, represented by 'x'.

Output Variables
The variables that a model predicts, represented by 'y'.

GE
Generalized Expectation framework.

Andrzejewski et al.
An entity that proposed a framework for incorporating general domain knowledge into LDA.<SEP>Proposed a framework in which general domain knowledge can be easily incorporated into LDA.

Altendorf et al.
An entity that explored monotonicity constraints for learning from sparse data.<SEP>Explored monotonicity constraints to improve the accuracy while learning from sparse data.

Chen et al.
Tried to learn comprehensible topic models by leveraging multi-domain knowledge.

Mann and McCallum
Incorporated labeled features and other knowledge like class distribution into the objective function of GE-FL, discussing from a semi-supervised perspective.

Raghavan et al.
Proposed to use feedback on instances and features interlacedly, demonstrating that feedback on features boosts the model.

This paper
Investigates into the problem of how to leverage prior knowledge robustly in learning models by proposing three regularization terms on top of generalized expectation criteria.

Regularization terms
Three terms proposed on top of generalized expectation criteria to leverage prior knowledge robustly in learning models.

Maximum entropy regularization
A regularization term showing strong ability to control unbalance, suitable when no corpus knowledge is available, but assumes uniform category distribution.

KL divergence
A regularization method that performs well on unbalanced corpora by utilizing the reference class distribution without assumptions, but requires providing the true class distribution.

True class distribution
The actual distribution of classes in a dataset.

Reference class distribution
A distribution of classes used for comparison or as a target in methods like KL divergence.

Figure 2
A figure displaying experimental results, specifically related to balanced and unbalanced datasets.

Figure 3
A figure showing experimental results on datasets with different unbalanced class distributions and features.

Figure 4
A figure illustrating the influence of lambda on a method incorporating KL divergence.

Table 1
A table presenting performance comparisons of different methods using LDA-selected features.

Liu et al.
An entity that manually labeled features for unsupervised clustering assignments.

Chang et al.
An entity that proposed constraint-driven learning.

Daumé
An entity that proposed a self-training method using cross-task knowledge constraints.

MaCallum et al.
An entity that proposed generalized expectation criteria.

Graça et al.
An entity that proposed the posterior regularization framework.

Unlabeled Instances
Instances within a dataset that do not have associated labels.

Constraint-Driven Learning
A learning approach guided by constraints.

Self-Training Method
A semi-supervised learning technique where a model is iteratively trained on its own predictions.

Posterior Regularization
A framework that projects a model's posterior onto distributions satisfying auxiliary constraints.

Monotonicity Constraints
Constraints that enforce a monotonic relationship between features and the target variable.

Positive Documents
Documents belonging to the positive class in a dataset.

Negative Documents
Documents belonging to the negative class in a dataset.

True Class Distribution
The actual distribution of classes in a dataset.

Control Group
A baseline group used for comparison in experiments.

Auxiliary Constraints
Additional constraints used in regularization frameworks.

Cross Task Knowledge Constraints
Knowledge constraints that apply across different tasks.

General Domain Knowledge
Broad knowledge applicable across various domains.

Sparse Data
Data characterized by a high proportion of zero or missing values.

Posterior
The posterior probability distribution of a model.

Features
LDA is used to select features.

Features of each topic
LDA selects the most probable features of each topic.

Labeled features
The reference distribution of labeled features is estimated using a heuristic strategy.

Reference distribution
The reference distribution of labeled features is estimated using a heuristic strategy.

Reference distributions
Neutral features have uniformly distributed reference distributions.

learns from
GE-FL uses labeled features and generalized expectation criteria for learning.

Top 10 frequent words
The top 10 frequent words are used as neutral features.

indicates
Model parameters indicate the importance of a word to a class.

expressed as
The model predicted distribution is expressed using a softmax function.

used for
L-BFGS is used for parameter estimation.

introduces
GE-FL introduces the KL divergence between reference and model predicted distributions into the objective function.

obtained by setting
The Generalized Expectation Criteria can be obtained by setting a specific constraint function.

prevent bias by setting to
Neutral features, when set to a uniform distribution, prevent model bias.

reduces
GE-FL reduces the load of instance annotation.

includes
The objective function includes a KL divergence term related to neutral features.

constrain
The maximum entropy principle is used to constrain the predicted class distribution on unlabeled data.

prevent
Neutral features prevent the model from biasing towards classes with a dominant number of labeled features.

performs well with
GE-FL performs well when provided with prior knowledge.

modified by
The objective function is modified by adding KL divergence between predicted and reference class distributions.

used in
The preference class distribution is used to modify the objective function.

represents
Model parameters represent the importance of a word to a class.

can be
Neutral features can be selected as the most common features.

can be expressed as
The model predicted distribution can be expressed as a softmax function.

defined by
GE-FL's objective function is defined by Equation 6.

used to solve
L-BFGS is used to solve the optimization problem for parameter estimation.

set to
Neutral features are set to a uniform distribution to prevent bias.

used to constrain
The Maximum Entropy Principle is used to constrain the predicted class distribution on unlabeled data.

used in modification of
The preference class distribution is used in the modification of the objective function.

between
KL divergence is calculated between the predicted and reference class distributions.

can be estimated without
Class distribution can be estimated without labeling instances.

can be taken as
Neutral features can be taken as the most common features.

reduces load of
GE-FL reduces the load of instance annotation.

Organization
Labeled features are used in sentiment classification as an example.

Generalized Expectation
Generalized expectation criteria directly constrain the model using constraint functions.

sparse data
Altendorf et al. learned from sparse data.

multi-domain knowledge
Chen et al. leveraged multi-domain knowledge to learn topic models.

features
Raghavan et al. proposed to use feedback on features.

semi-supervised perspective
Mann and McCallum discussed their work from a semi-supervised perspective.

labels on features
Druck et al. proposed an active learning method which solicits labels on features.

prior knowledge
This paper investigates how to leverage prior knowledge robustly.

generalized expectation criteria
The regularization terms are proposed on top of generalized expectation criteria.

model
Feedback on features boosts the model, as demonstrated by Raghavan et al.

unbalance
The maximum entropy regularization term shows the strong ability of controlling unbalance.

unbalanced corpora
The KL divergence performs much better on unbalanced corpora than other methods.

extremely unbalanced labeled features
Neutral features are not strong enough to handle extremely unbalanced labeled features.

corpus
This method is suitable when we know nothing about the corpus.

reference class distribution
KL divergence utilizes the reference class distribution.

category distribution
This method assumes that the categories are uniformly distributed.

true class distribution

true distribution

Our methods
Our methods are evaluated on movie datasets with unbalanced class distributions.

Figure 3 (b)
Our methods significantly outperform GE-FL in Figure 3 (b).

LDA does not consider class balance among classes when selecting features.

Bias Problem
Our methods introduce regularization terms to control the bias problem.

Daumé proposed a self-training method.

Learning
